items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the education law, in relation to grant awards for
conservation and preservation of library research materials
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S6938

SPONSOR: CHU
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the education law, in relation to grant awards for
conservation and preservation of library research materials

 
PURPOSE OF THE BILL:

The proposed legislation would provide for the administration of grant
awards for conservation and preservation of library research materials
during a school year, rather than a state fiscal year.

 
SUMMARY OF THE PROVISIONS OF THE BILL:

Section 1 of the bill would amend Education Law § 273(6) to require that
grant awards for conservation and preservation of library research mate-
rials be administered during a "school year", rather than a "state
fiscal year". Education § 2(15) defines the term "school year" as "the
period commencing on the first day of July in each year and ending on
the thirtieth day of June next following."

Section 2 is the effective date.

 
STATEMENT IN SUPPORT OF THE BILL:

Education Law § 273(6) requires that each fiscal year the Commissioner
award an annual formal grant of $158,000 to certain comprehensive
research libraries for a program of conservation and/or preservation of
library research materials. All of the comprehensive research libraries
that receive such grant operate on an academic fiscal year.  Some of
these institutions, such as the State University of New York at Albany
library, have their grant funds frozen from April first until they
receive their approval for the next program year in July.  As a result,
such libraries lose the first three months of possible spending and
continue to spend previous year's grant funding which has been carried
over, which complicates their grant application and reporting. Aligning
this grant funding schedule with the academic fiscal year will allow a
greater period for these libraries to spend their awards and simplify
their applications and reporting.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

This is a new bill.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act would take effect immediately.
